narrative: The technology landscape sees rapid advancements and critical challenges: AI continues its brisk pace with new model releases from Google and OpenAI, sparking both excitement for enhanced capabilities and alarm among safety experts over advanced reasoning techniques and potential security vulnerabilities. Simultaneously, Uber is making strategic global shifts, launching robotaxis in London and pursuing a major acquisition while undergoing significant layoffs and market exits. Data security and privacy remain paramount concerns, highlighted by a large-scale ID verification service breach and ongoing legal debates regarding AI's use of copyrighted material.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts
highlights.whyItMatters: OpenAI's upcoming Astra model uses 'recurrent depth,' a new reasoning technique causing alarm among safety experts who fear it may be a significant step back for AI security/safety.

highlights.title: Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London
highlights.whyItMatters: Uber has launched London's first commercial robotaxi service using Wayve's autonomous driving technology, marking a significant milestone for urban autonomous transportation in a major global city.

highlights.title: It sure looks like hackers breached a major ID card verification service
highlights.whyItMatters: Reports indicate a massive data breach involving over 150 million driver's license photos from a major ID verification service, raising serious privacy and security concerns about personal identity data.

highlights.title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
highlights.whyItMatters: The US government has intervened in The New York Times lawsuit, arguing in favor of OpenAI's right to train LLMs on copyrighted material, which could significantly influence future AI development and intellectual property debates.

highlights.title: Google spared from ad-business breakup, but judge orders changes to how it operates
highlights.whyItMatters: Google avoided a breakup of its advertising business in an antitrust case, but a judge ordered operational changes to benefit competitors, signaling ongoing regulatory pressure and market adjustments for tech giants.

highlights.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
highlights.whyItMatters: RonanRx, a new YC-backed pharmaceutical company, aims to vertically integrate the entire process for personalized GLP-1s and peptides, from manufacturing to delivery, making treatments more affordable and tailored.

topics.name: Artificial Intelligence
topics.summary: Rapid advancements continue with new models from OpenAI (Astra) and Google (Gemini 3.8 Flash), though safety experts raise alarms about advanced reasoning techniques and potential security risks. The US government supports OpenAI in copyrighted training, while Amazon introduces AI for scam detection. Enterprise AI security sees significant investment, and new AI terminology emerges.

topics.name: Transportation & Mobility
topics.summary: Uber makes headlines with the launch of its first commercial robotaxi service in London, a potential $15B takeover bid for Delivery Hero, and a significant 10% staff layoff, alongside exiting Nigeria and Uganda. The new Range Rover EV is unveiled, emphasizing familiar design.

topics.name: Cybersecurity & Data Privacy
topics.summary: A major ID card verification service suffered a breach exposing over 150 million driver's license photos, alongside reports of a BGP hijack causing network infections. The FCC plans a robocall scorecard, and Norway considers banning camera-enabled wearables due to privacy risks.

topics.name: Business & Startups
topics.summary: Palo Alto Networks acquired Console for $500M, while Adobe made two acquisitions (Rilo, Rephrase.ai). TechCrunch Disrupt announced stages focused on scaling startups and Real World AI. RonanRx launched a vertically integrated personalized pharma company.

topics.name: Space & Science
topics.summary: NASA announced Blue Origin as the provider for Mars Telecommunications Network, adjusted lunar spacesuit designs for Artemis IV, and continues Hubble observations. Several other science stories cover dark matter, aging brains, and space history.
